identity.real_world_identity_notes: Aston Martin describes the competition Valkyrie as a non-hybrid Le Mans Hypercar with a seven-speed sequential semi-automatic paddle-shift transmission. AMS2 places the exact telemetry identity in class LMDh. No exact Low Downforce telemetry identity was observed or approved.

wheel_rim.notes: Direct AMS2 cockpit inspection showed a closed GT/Formula rim with an integrated display; exact diameter remains unknown.

notes: With Auto Clutch disabled, AMS2 1.6.9.91 moved the car from rest without physical clutch input. The simulator mechanism was not established and must not be described as electric launch because the competition Valkyrie is non-hybrid.
All seven forward gears were selected by paddles, and clutch-free full-throttle upshifts were accepted with a perceptible automatic cut.
Clutch-free downshifts were accepted with the driver's foot off the throttle, and automatic blip was directly visible as a throttle-display spike.
Only the exact base telemetry identity was observed. No Low Downforce alias is introduced by this record.
Live-tested in AMS2 1.6.9.91 with Auto Clutch disabled.

Clutch-free move-off, seven paddle-selected gears, no-lift clutch-free upshifts with automatic cut, clutch-free downshifts with automatic blip, and a closed GT/Formula display rim were directly observed.
The mechanism behind clutch-free move-off remains unknown; the non-hybrid car is not characterized as using electric launch.

confidence.basis: Exact identity and the complete user-facing control technique were directly checked in AMS2; Aston Martin independently establishes the seven-speed sequential semi-automatic paddle hardware.

claims.basis: Official addition plus the exact live telemetry name and LMDh class observed through SimHub 9.11.22.
Manufacturer sources specify a seven-speed sequential semi-automatic paddle transmission, and all seven paddle-selected gears were exercised in AMS2.

Direct testing established clutch-free move-off, full-throttle clutch-free upshifts with perceptible cut, and clutch-free downshifts with a visible automatic-blip spike. The move-off mechanism remains explicitly unknown.
Direct cockpit inspection showed a closed GT/Formula rim with an integrated display; the manufacturer source independently documents the closely related display wheel.

notes: This record deliberately distinguishes the non-hybrid competition Valkyrie from LMDh cars that can move under electric power.
No Low Downforce telemetry alias is approved because no exact distinct identity was observed.

The wheel-rim shape was originally recorded as "prototype", a value that named a racing category rather than a rim outline. That value is retired: the rims it covered are the same closed form, flattened at both the top and the bottom, that the project now records as "gt-style". The shape was remapped by definition and the rim was not observed again.

The wheel-rim shape was originally recorded as "gt-style". The separate "gt-style", "formula" and "prototype" values described the same rim: molded grips at 9 and 3 with a control face between them, usually carrying a display and rev lights. They are merged into "gt-formula". The rim was not observed again and nothing about the observation changed.
